title: Basel III: international regulatory framework for banks
summary: This BIS page is a navigational index listing Basel III regulatory publications and documents, not substantive research content. It references the post-crisis regulatory reforms finalized in December 2017 and January 2019, which strengthened bank capital requirements, liquidity standards, and market risk frameworks for internationally active banks.
key_points: The Basel III reforms were developed by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision in response to the 2007-09 financial crisis
Key components include Minimum capital requirements for market risk (January 2016, revised January 2019), Liquidity Coverage Ratio (January 2013), and Net Stable Funding Ratio (October 2014)
Post-crisis regulatory reforms were endorsed by the Group of Governors and Heads of Supervision (GHOS) on 7 December 2017
Adjustments to the market risk framework were endorsed by GHOS on 14 January 2019
Basel III standards are minimum requirements applying to internationally active banks
Transitional arrangements for Basel III implementation span 2017-2028
why_it_matters: This page serves as a directory to Basel III documentation but provides no new information. The actual Basel III reforms affect bank capital requirements and risk management, which indirectly influences market structure through bank behavior in fixed income and derivatives markets.
market_structure_context: Basel III capital and market risk requirements affect how banks structure their trading operations and the cost of market-making activities, but this listing page contains no specific market structure analysis or data.
